analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sporting (10th, 9 points) won 1-0 at Shakhtar on matchday 4, while Manchester United (17th, 6 points) beat Roma 3-2 after being 2-0 down, then drew 4-4 with Aston Villa. United are in the Premier League relegation zone and ESPN sources say the club is weighing Michael Carrick's future, so the manager could change before this game. Matheus Cunha, who scored twice against Roma, is banned after his second yellow card in that game (ban not yet served).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and I lean higher. United's last two games produced 13 goals (3-2 against Roma, 4-4 against Villa), and their defence is very open. Sporting kept a clean sheet in Ukraine, but United without Cunha still have Bruno Fernandes, who scored against Roma.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Sporting should have more of the ball at home, but United create most of their chances in transition rather than from sustained pressure. I stay with the estimate.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and I lean slightly higher. United picked up five yellow cards and a red against Roma, and a team under heavy pressure tends to concede fouls. Sporting had only one player booked at Shakhtar, so most of the cards may go to United.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. United's recent games have been very open, but some of that was due to their own comebacks, which may not be repeated in Lisbon. I stay with the estimate.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. Sporting will create good chances against an open United defence, but Cunha's absence reduces United's threat. I see no reason to move the figure.
